title: Product of signs over a fiber
statement: Let $n,m$ be natural numbers, let $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, let $\pi:\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$, let $w$ be an $m$-tuple of signs, and choose $j\in\{0,\ldots,m-1\}$. The product of the sign at $j$ over all $i\in S$ with $\pi(i)=j$ equals that sign if the number of such indices is odd, and equals $1$ otherwise.
hypotheses_covered: $S$ is a finite subset of the $n$ coordinates
$\pi$ maps the $n$ coordinates to the $m$ coordinates
